## Multiple Choice Questions

**1.** In a relational database, which of the following best describes the role of a primary key?

A.  It uniquely identifies each row and cannot be duplicated or blank.
B.  It stores the most important data value in the table.
C.  It connects one table to another by referencing a column in a different table.
D.  It defines the data type for all columns in the table.

**2.** The CustomerID column appears in both the Charles River Customer table and the SalesOrder table. In the SalesOrder table, this column functions as a:

A.  Primary key
B.  Foreign key
C.  Composite key
D.  Data type

**3.** An ER diagram shows a line between two tables. The line has a single bar on one end and a crow's foot on the other end. Ignoring optionality, this notation represents which type of relationship?

A.  One-to-one
B.  One-to-many
C.  Many-to-many
D.  The notation does not indicate cardinality

**4.** The Charles River SalesOrderLine table contains foreign keys to both SalesOrder and Item. This table exists because:

A.  It stores the primary key of the SalesOrder table.
B.  It is required for every database to have at least one table with two foreign keys.
C.  It stores customer contact information for each order.
D.  It resolves a many-to-many relationship between sales orders and items.

**5.** A cost accountant wants to compare standard item costs to actual production costs and analyze manufacturing variances. Which Charles River table group is best suited for this analysis?

A.  The O2C group, because it contains product pricing data in SalesOrderLine
B.  The Accounting Core group, because it contains a complete general ledger
C.  The Manufacturing group, whose completions and closes hold standard costs and variances
D.  The Master Data group, because the Item table contains the StandardCost and ListPrice columns

**6.** In the Charles River database, the Account table contains a column called ParentAccountID that references another row in the same Account table. This is an example of a:

A.  Foreign key referencing a different table
B.  Cross-group bridge key
C.  Self-referencing relationship
D.  Many-to-many relationship

**7.** An auditor wants to prepare a trial balance directly from the Charles River database. Which tables provide the necessary data?

A.  Account and GLEntry from the Accounting Core group
B.  SalesOrder and SalesOrderLine from the O2C group
C.  WorkOrder and ProductionCompletion from the Manufacturing group
D.  Item and Warehouse from the Master Data group

**8.** The Charles River SQLite file declares a primary key for every table but declares no foreign key constraints. What does this mean for an analyst who plans to join SalesOrder to Customer?

A.  The join will fail because the relationship is not declared in the file.
B.  The database automatically prevents orphaned orders, so the analyst does not need to test anything.
C.  The join still works, but the analyst should test that every CustomerID matches a customer.
D.  CustomerID must first be converted to text before the two tables can be joined.

**9.** A relational database enforces referential integrity. This means that:

A.  Every table must contain at least one foreign key.
B.  Primary key values can be duplicated, as long as the duplicate values appear in different tables of the database.
C.  Tables without relationships are automatically deleted from the database.
D.  Every foreign key value that is not blank matches an existing primary key in the referenced table.

**10.** An analyst joins the Charles River Customer table to SalesOrder and then to SalesOrderLine. One customer has 10 orders, and those 10 orders contain a total of 45 line items. How many rows will this customer contribute to the joined result?

A.  1 row
B.  10 rows
C.  45 rows
D.  55 rows

**11.** Which of the following accounting structures is represented in a database as a self-referencing table where child rows point to parent rows within the same table?

A.  The chart of accounts hierarchy
B.  The general ledger
C.  The trial balance
D.  The accounts receivable sub-ledger

**12.** The Charles River GLEntry table uses SourceDocumentType and SourceDocumentID to link general ledger entries to their source documents. This design differs from a standard foreign key because:

A.  It uses two columns instead of one.
B.  It points to a different table depending on SourceDocumentType, so no one foreign key describes it.
C.  It stores the amount of the source document in the ledger row rather than the key of that document.
D.  It is used only for manual journal entries, and not for invoices, payments, or other transaction types.

**13.** Which of the following is the best definition of a relational database?

A.  A system that stores data in tables linked by primary and foreign keys
B.  A database that keeps all of its data together in one single large table
C.  A spreadsheet with multiple worksheets
D.  A database whose data can be read and changed only by writing SQL statements

**14.** In a database that enforces data types, a column defined as INTEGER could store which of the following values?

A.  "Accounts Receivable"
B.  2024-03-15
C.  99.73
D.  4500

**15.** The Charles River Master Data group has only a few tables, while the Order-to-Cash group is the largest table group in the database. Which of the following best explains this difference?

A.  The O2C group is a newer part of the database and uses more modern design principles.
B.  The O2C cycle has many stages, from pricing to cash collection, and each one needs its own tables.
C.  The Master Data group contains errors that should have been stored in additional tables.
D.  The number of tables is arbitrary and has no relationship to the complexity of the business process.
